author: danielgorgonha
body:
## Changes

- A gRPC status sent in the body trailer frame now reaches the caller. The vendored `tonic-web-wasm-client` 0.8.0 parsed the trailer frame and then dropped it, so tonic never saw the trailers, and tonic 0.14.3 (the locked version) treats HTTP 200 with no trailers as success. A stream that failed part-way looked complete, a unary call that returned a message followed by an error status looked successful, and an error sent with no message before it became an empty successful stream.
- Example from a public endpoint: `zcash-mainnet.chainsafe.dev` answers `GetBlock` for a height past the tip with HTTP 200, no `grpc-status` header, and a body that is a single trailer frame with `grpc-status: 11`. Today a unary call on that body fails with `Internal: Missing response message.` instead of the server's status, and the same body read as a server stream is an empty success. With this change both get `OutOfRange: GetBlock: block 999999999 is newer than the latest block`. The body, captured on 2026-11-15, is a test fixture here.
- The body counts as finished only once the trailer frame has been read in full. A trailer frame split across chunks is now read, and a response cut inside it is `MalformedResponse` instead of a clean end. Unchanged: trailers-only responses (status in the HTTP headers, empty body), and a body that ends with no trailer frame (still `MalformedResponse`).
- Where it comes from: the forwarding is the `src/response_body.rs` change of devashishdxt/tonic-web-wasm-client#90 (upstream 0f232d33, released in 0.9.1). The split-trailer case is upstream issue devashishdxt/tonic-web-wasm-client#97, and the open upstream PR devashishdxt/tonic-web-wasm-client#112 makes the same change to the end-of-body check (only `Done` counts as finished); it is not merged. This workspace cannot take 0.9.x: every 0.9.x release depends on `wasm-streams` 0.5 or later, which requires `wasm-bindgen >= 0.2.108`, against the `=0.2.100` pin kept for the MetaMask Snap.
- `VENDORED.md` describes both local fixes. `trailers.patch` applies on top of `trailers-only.patch` and reproduces `src/` from crates.io 0.8.0, apart from the test files (the patch carries only their two `cfg(test)` hooks).
- New CI job `vendored-tonic-web-wasm-client`: the crate is excluded from the workspace, so `--all` never built its tests.
- Why now: tonic 0.14.6 and later report HTTP 200 with no trailers as an error. With tonic 0.14.6 in a scratch lock, the captured successful unary body fails with `Unknown: protocol error: missing grpc-status trailer, ...` before this change and succeeds after it. So without this fix, a `cargo update` of tonic breaks every call that has a body.

Behaviour that changes for apps: an error that a server sends in the body trailer now fails the call, where before it was silently dropped. In a normal sync we saw no difference: a read-only sync of the last 200 blocks, with a new account, completed to the tip both before and after this change, against `https://zjs.zec.rocks/testnet` (testnet), `https://zcash-mainnet.chainsafe.dev` (mainnet) and `https://zjs.zec.rocks/mainnet` (the web wallet's mainnet proxy), in headless Chromium with the threaded build.

Other behaviour changes: a trailer block that does not parse now fails with `HeaderParsingError` whether it arrives in one chunk or split (before, the split case ended silently). Body trailers now reach tonic, and tonic 0.14.3 panics on an invalid `grpc-status-details-bin` (`Status::from_header_map` decodes it with `expect`): a server could already trigger that through the HTTP headers, and now it can also do so through the body trailer.

Known and not changed: `grpc-status: 0` in the headers together with an error in a body trailer still reports success; repeated trailer keys keep only the last value (upstream #103); bytes after the trailer frame are ignored; base64 (`grpc-web-text`) mode is not used here; like a data frame, a trailer frame is buffered until its announced length has arrived.

The problem was found, reproduced and first fixed by @Crackdevs in their browser OHTTP proof, built on this branch (https://github.com/Crackdevs/zcash-browser-ohttp-proof): their `wallet.patch` already makes the decoder pass the trailers to tonic and require a complete trailer frame. That repository has no licence file, so none of their code is used here; this patch was written separately, from the upstream change named above. If they open their own pull request, we will close this one in its favour. The analysis and the patch were prepared with an AI assistant and reviewed by us.

## Tests

```
cargo test --locked -p tonic-web-wasm-client
```

15 tests (14 new). The first commit adds the tests, a `cfg(test)` constructor that feeds the body from in-memory chunks, and moves the body of `ResponseBody::new` into a private `from_body_stream` (no change in behaviour). On that commit, 8 fail (trailers never yielded, split trailers, end inside the trailer frame, tonic streaming and unary calls, the captured body). With the fix, all 15 pass. The guards (trailers-only empty body, trailers-only with a truncated body, data with no trailer, cut inside a data frame, captured successful body, nothing after the trailers) pass on both commits.

## Issues

- Based on #27: the vendored crate this changes exists only on that branch, not on `main`. I can retarget to `main` once #27 lands, or fold this into #27, whichever you prefer.
- Upstream: devashishdxt/tonic-web-wasm-client#97, devashishdxt/tonic-web-wasm-client#112.
